article.title: The Two Cities Ledger
article.description: Ravi Teja Varma's (34, engineering manager) relocation from Hyderabad's Financial District to Bengaluru's ORR — a ₹2.4 Cr budget that bought premium in Kokapet and decent in Whitefield, a Section 54 clock, and a spec-adjusted path to peace.
article.quote: "In Hyderabad this is 40% cheaper. I know. Everyone knows. Stop telling me."

learnings.text: Section 54 rewards under-construction primary purchases — the reinvestment timeline accommodates construction-linked payments if structured correctly
Spec-adjusted comparison (UDS, parking, maintenance) narrows the '40% cheaper' headline to 28% — grief becomes accurate, which oddly helps
The premium is real and has a name: the job market that rescued his career twice — insurance has premiums

quotes.text: In Hyderabad this is 40% cheaper. I know. Everyone knows. Stop telling me.

quotes.text: Wealth where we aren't, tenancy where we are.
quotes.author: — Spandana

quotes.text: Your model wins on XIRR, Ravi. It loses on address — the place your daughter says when someone asks where she's from.
quotes.author: — Riya

quotes.text: The premium's real name is the job market that rescued your career twice.
quotes.author: — Riya

chatMessages.text: Riya, asalu listen to this model, it's beautiful. Buy in Kokapet — nine-five per square foot, my home market, I KNOW those streets — rent here in Whitefield. Arbitrage, kada?
It's a clean model. Can I add one row your spreadsheet is missing? Row forty-seven: 'Spandana's answer.' Wealth where we aren't, tenancy where we are. Your model wins on XIRR — it loses on address.

tabs.insightTitle: What I noticed while we were searching
tabs.insightDescription: “Ravi Teja wasn't comparing flats; he was comparing lives, and the spreadsheet had no tab for that. Every visit came with a Kokapet price-ghost in the room, so we priced the ghost: UDS, parking, maintenance — the 40% headline shrank to 28%, which is still real but survivable. And when the buy-there-rent-here model looked perfect, Spandana's one sentence ended it: wealth where we aren't, tenancy where we are. The premium wasn't bubble — it was the job market that rescued his career twice. Insurance has premiums. He paid it, inside the window, and the ledger's weather row finally wrote 'Bengaluru wins.'”

tabs.adviceDescription: For inter-city movers, the grief is itemized before the decision — and that's an asset. Run the spec-adjusted comparison early so the pain is accurate, let the CA decode the Section 54 window before the forums do, and rename the city premium honestly: the deeper job market is career insurance with a premium, not a bubble to out-wait. Ravi Teja and Spandana proved that when the premium has a name, the comparison loop ends — and the deed gets registered inside the window.
